title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning to reduce queueing unfairness and prevent starvation (priority aging, timeouts)
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: production traces showed intermittent request starvation for low-priority clients during sustained high QPS. The continuous-batcher scheduler can favor hot prefixes and large batched groups which, under skewed workload mixes, leads to unbounded queueing for thinly-sporadic clients. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve fairness and add explicit starvation prevention/timeouts. Summary: 1) Add priority aging: requests escalate their effective priority proportional to waiting time within a sliding fairness window. 2) Introduce per-request starvation timeout: requests older than X ms are promoted into an urgent lane and guaranteed next-batch dispatch. 3) Queue-slot accounting: track reserved slots per logical client to prevent large groups from monopolizing batch capacity. 4) Backpressure/early-reject heuristics when queueing exceeds SLO thresholds to avoid cascading latency. 5) Expose new metrics and traces for queued_time_buckets, promoted_by_age, starvation_promotions, reserved_slots_in_use. 6) Add unit and integration tests and microbenchmarks to validate behavior under synthetic skewed workloads and real traces. Compatibility: changes are backward compatible at the API level; tuning is default-on but guarded by a feature flag continuous_batcher.fairness_v2 for quick rollback. Risk/rollback: small risk of performance regression for extremely cold workloads; rollout plan includes gradual rollout with metric gates. See linked Linear tasks ENG-4123 and ENG-4178 for evaluation/rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and perf hypothesis - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks - [x] Feature flag and rollout gates - [x] Observability additions - [x] Merge and release notes

diff_snippets:
--- a/services/continuous_batcher/scheduler.py +++ b/services/continuous_batcher/scheduler.py def schedule_next(batch_slots):
-    # previous FIFO/coalescing heuristic
-    candidates = pick_best_prefixes(batch_slots)
+    # new fairness: compute effective priority = base_priority + aging_factor * wait_time_ms
+    candidates = pick_best_prefixes_with_aging(batch_slots)

+    # Starvation promotion: any request with queued_ms >= STARVATION_TIMEOUT gets urgent lane
+    if req.queued_ms >= STARVATION_TIMEOUT_MS:
+        promote_to_urgent_lane(req)

+    # Track reserved slots per client to limit monopolization
+    reserved_slots_by_client[client_id] += reserved_for_this_group

release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduling fairness by adding priority aging, starvation promotion, and per-client slot accounting. Reduces p99 queueing latency under skewed workloads and prevents long-tail starvation. Rollout behind feature flag. See ENG-4123/ENG-4178 for dashboards and rollout plan.
benchmarks_summary: Skewed synthetic workload (70% hot, 30% sporadic): p99 latency improved 10%
Sustained high QPS with mixed clients: starvation incidents reduced from 14/10k requests to 0/10k
End-to-end throughput nominally unchanged (<1% reduction in p50 under extreme tuning)
observability_changes: traces: scheduler.queueing_event span tags for promotion_reason
risk_and_rollback: Default behavior is behind continuous_batcher.fairness_v2 feature flag. If rollout shows regressions we will disable the flag globally and revert the scheduler tuning commit. We will monitor p99 latency, promotion_rate, and reserved_slots_in_use during rollout. Rollback path validated in integration tests.
